item.title: Iran war impact slows global growth and intensifies inflation pressures, business surveys show
item.description: The Iran war is already taking a toll on major economies around the world, according to business surveys on Tuesday which showed how a ​surge in energy prices and rising uncertainty were dampening activity and pushing inflation expectations higher.

item.title: Hudson County Community College Generates Substantial Economic Impact Across the Area, Study Finds
item.description: Attaining a certificate or degree from Hudson County Community College (HCCC) results in generous financial returns for alumni, individuals and businesses throughout the region.

item.title: OpenAI Foundation pledges $1B in grants to ensure AI ‘benefits all of humanity’
item.description: OpenAI Foundation, the nonprofit that controls the artificial intelligence company OpenAI and its flagship product ChatGPT, pledged to grant out $1 billion over the next year and to build up its capacity as a philanthropic funder.

item.title: U.S. fourth-quarter productivity growth revised down, but trend remains solid
item.description: U.S. worker productivity growth slowed more than initially thought in the fourth quarter, but the trend remained solid and could get a boost from the rapid adoption of ​artificial intelligence by businesses.

item.title: U.S. business activity slips to 11-month low in March amid Iran war, S&P Global survey shows
item.description: U.S. business activity slowed to an 11-month low in March as the war in the Middle ​East raised prices for energy products and other inputs, a survey showed on Tuesday, reinforcing fears of an ‌acceleration in inflation in the months ahead.

item.title: It’s a bad time to hunt for new jobs, most U.S. workers say in new Gallup poll
item.description: Americans’ outlook on the job market has turned increasingly pessimistic, a surprisingly negative shift given the low unemployment rate but one that likely reflects an ongoing hiring drought.

item.title: U.S. menus are replacing spirits with cheaper options due to the impact of Trump’s tariffs
item.description: Certain champagne and cremant brands that were once wine menu staples are on the chopping block at restaurants and bars owned by New York-based Kent Hospitality Group, says wine director Kristen Goceljak.

item.title: Wealthy investors are betting on women’s sports because of their rapid growth and lower prices
item.description: Wealthy investors are increasingly turning to women's sports as a rare opportunity to tap into a fast-growing market at lower valuations, favoring strong returns over the high entry costs and limited upside of marquee men's franchises in the NFL or the UK's Premier League.

item.title: No more excuses: World Cup pressure is on for host USA
item.description: The last time the United States hosted the World Cup, Bill Clinton was in the White House, Nirvana was on the radio, and most Americans couldn't name a single player on their national team.

item.title: Summer Fancy Food Show 2026 to Bring Thousands of Buyers and Gourmet Brands to New York
item.description: The Summer Fancy Food Show 2026, considered North America’s leading specialty food product discovery event, will take place from June 28 to June 30 at the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center in New York City.
